title: Is Factuality Enhancement a Free Lunch For LLMs? Better Factuality Can Lead to Worse Context-Faithfulness

contributions.purpose: Determine whether popular LLM factuality-enhancement methods actually improve factual accuracy, and how reliably.
contributions.mechanism: Re-evaluation of a range of factuality-enhancement methods (contrastive-decoding methods like DoLa/CD/ICD and representation-editing methods like ITI/TruthX) on standard factuality benchmarks, comparing against an unmodified decoding baseline.
contributions.evaluation: On TruthfulQA and FACTScore with LLAMA2-7B/13B-CHAT, improvements are modest, unstable, and inconsistent across metrics; some methods decline on some metrics (red-marked in Table 1) relative to baseline.
contributions.source_quote: We first revisit the current factuality enhancement methods and evaluate their effectiveness in enhancing factual accuracy... while these methods may yield inconsistent improvements in factual accuracy,

contributions.purpose: Show that improving factuality comes at a hidden cost: it damages LLMs' context-faithfulness (ability to follow injected/updated context).
contributions.mechanism: Evaluation of the same factuality-enhancement methods on knowledge-editing tasks (in-context editing / ICE on MQUAKE, plus MeLLo), using editing accuracy as a proxy for context-faithfulness, against the LLAMA2-CHAT baseline.
contributions.evaluation: All methods decline vs baseline on ICE without exception (avg decrease >20%); largest reported drop 69.7% (TruthX up to 67.9% on ICE, 60.3% cited in intro); with MeLLo most declines exceed 40%, worse for larger models.
contributions.source_quote: The experimental results reveal that while these methods may yield inconsistent improvements in factual accuracy, they also cause a more severe decline in context-faithfulness, with the largest decrease reaching a striking 69.7%.

contributions.purpose: Mechanistically explain why factuality enhancement degrades context-faithfulness.
contributions.mechanism: A custom knowledge-token capturing algorithm plus analysis of logit distributions and hidden states for new-knowledge vs parametric-knowledge tokens before/after context injection (2,000 QA instances on MQUAKE-STUBBORN); case study classifying unfaithful outputs.
contributions.evaluation: After context injection, hidden states stay concentrated near original parametric outputs; logits for new-knowledge tokens drop while parametric-knowledge logits rise; representation-editing methods (esp. TruthX) most restrict hidden-state dispersion, explaining their largest faithfulness declines.
contributions.source_quote: To explain these declines, we analyze the hidden states and logit distributions for the tokens representing new knowledge and parametric knowledge respectively, highlighting the limitations of current approaches.

notes: Entire paper is a negative/trade-off result: the central claim is that factuality enhancement is NOT a free lunch, it significantly undermines context-faithfulness (avg >20% ICE drop, up to 69.7%; MeLLo drops >40%). Additional trade-off noted: adding CoT helps the baseline but is unstable and mostly hurts factuality-enhanced models. All method categories (training/inference/prompt-based) affected without exception. No new method proposed; contribution is diagnostic + recommendation for future work to balance factuality and context-faithfulness.
